chunks: And Sama'ah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
False witnesses are flogged as a punishment, and it has no fixed measure; that is left to the Imam. And they are paraded so that they may be recognized and not return to it.
He said: I said, 'Then if they repent and reform, will their testimony be accepted afterward?' So he said:
If they repent, Allah accepts their repentance, and their testimony is accepted afterward.

key_terms.أَصْلَحُوا: they reformed; they corrected their conduct
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam; the authority who determines the extent of the punishment here
key_terms.تَابُوا: they repented; they turned back from the sin
key_terms.حَدّاً: a penal punishment imposed as a legal sanction
key_terms.شُهُودُ الزُّورِ: false witnesses; those who give untruthful testimony
key_terms.يُجْلَدُونَ: they are flogged; they receive corporal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on false witnesses, and is their testimony accepted after repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning false testimony: those who bear false witness are punished, and the extent of the punishment is left to the Imam. It also establishes that if such people sincerely repent and reform, their testimony may later be accepted again.
